lead: Almost every organ system changes in pregnancy, mainly under progesterone (relaxes smooth muscle) and oestrogen (growth, plasma proteins, clotting factors). The changes supply the fetus and prepare the mother for blood loss at delivery, and they return to normal within about 6 weeks after birth. Knowing them stops normal findings being mistaken for disease.
f: Genital tract

Uterus 50–70 g → about 1000 g at term; hypertrophy early, stretching later · Braxton Hicks contractions from mid-pregnancy: painless, do not open the cervix · Isthmus forms the lower uterine segment in the third trimester · Cervix soft (Goodell's sign), mucus plug · Vagina bluish (Chadwick's sign, about 8 wk); leucorrhoea; candida more common
Cardiovascular changes

Cardiac output +40%: stroke volume first, then heart rate +10–15 · Most of the rise by 20–24 wk; highest just after delivery · Heart failure risk peaks at 24–28 wk, in labour and just after delivery · Uterine blood flow 500–750 mL/min at term: why PPH kills in minutes · Peripheral resistance falls: BP lowest in the second trimester, back to booking level by term · IVC compression: ankle oedema, varicose veins, haemorrhoids · Supine hypotension after 20 wk: prevent with a 15° left lateral tilt · Apex in the 4th space, ejection systolic murmur and third sound are normal · A diastolic murmur is never normal

sc: Feels faint lying flat at 32 wk → Supine hypotension: left lateral tilt

f: Haematological changes

Plasma volume +45%, red cell mass +25%: Hb about 11 g/dL with normal MCV = physiological anaemia · Iron need about 1000 mg · WBC up to 15 × 10⁹/L (higher in labour); platelets slightly lower · ESR normally high: not useful · Hypercoagulable: fibrinogen and factors VII, VIII, X rise; protein S falls; less fibrinolysis · VTE risk 4–6 times, highest after delivery

sc: Hb 11.2 g/dL at 30 wk, MCV 88 fL → Haemodilution: physiological anaemia

f: Respiratory changes

Progesterone drives breathing: tidal volume +40%, minute ventilation +40–50%, respiratory rate unchanged · pCO₂ falls to about 30 mmHg (4 kPa): compensated respiratory alkalosis · Oxygen use +20%, FRC −20%: quick hypoxia at induction, so pre-oxygenate · Physiological breathlessness in up to 70%: at rest or talking, normal SpO₂ · Breathless on mild effort, at night or with low SpO₂: look for anaemia, heart disease, PE

tr: A fast respiratory rate is a sign of illness, not of pregnancy
A 'normal' pCO₂ of 40 mmHg in an asthmatic pregnant woman means she is tiring

f: Renal and urinary tract

Renal plasma flow +50–75%, GFR +50%: creatinine, urea and uric acid fall · Creatinine above 75 µmol/L suggests kidney disease · Glycosuria is common: confirm diabetes with a blood test (OGTT) · Protein up to 300 mg/24 h is normal · Dilated ureters, right more than left: asymptomatic bacteriuria → pyelonephritis in 20–30% if untreated: screen all women · Frequency early and near term
Gastrointestinal and liver

Nausea peaks at 8–12 wk (hCG), settles by 16–20 wk · Heartburn; slow gastric emptying in labour: aspiration risk under general anaesthesia · Constipation, gingivitis, gallstones more common · ALP rises 2–4 times (placental): normal · Albumin falls; total calcium falls, ionised normal · ALT, bilirubin and bile acids do not rise: if raised, think obstetric cholestasis, AFLP, HELLP or hepatitis

sc: ALT 120 IU/L with itching at 34 wk → Obstetric cholestasis

f: Placental hormones and endocrine changes

hCG (syncytiotrophoblast) keeps the corpus luteum until the placenta takes over at 8–10 wk; very high in molar and twin pregnancy · hPL rises with placental size: insulin resistance in the second half · Progesterone: heartburn, constipation, dilated ureters · Relaxin: loose pelvic joints · Thyroid: TBG doubles, total T4 rises, free T4 normal; TSH low in the first trimester (hCG) · Pituitary doubles (prolactin cells): Sheehan's syndrome after massive PPH · Gestational diabetes appears at 24–28 wk: screening time · Reduced cell-mediated immunity: severe malaria, varicella, hepatitis E

sc: Low TSH, normal free T4 in the first trimester → Normal (hCG effect): no treatment
High total T4, normal free T4 and TSH at 16 wk → Raised thyroxine-binding globulin

f: Skin, breasts and musculoskeletal

Linea nigra, chloasma (worse in sunlight), striae gravidarum (red-purple now, silvery later) · Spider naevi, palmar erythema: fade after delivery · Breasts tender from 6 wk; Montgomery's tubercles; colostrum from mid-pregnancy · Symphysis pain, backache, lordosis, carpal tunnel syndrome · Hair falls out 2–4 months after delivery

tr: Itching of the palms and soles without a rash is not dry skin: check bile acids

f: Weight gain

About 12.5 kg in a normal-weight woman, about 0.5 kg a week in the second half · Recommended gain by booking BMI: under 18.5: 12.5–18 kg; 18.5–24.9: 11.5–16 kg; 25–29.9: 7–11.5 kg; 30 or more: 5–9 kg · Fetus 3.5 kg, placenta 0.7, liquor 0.8, uterus 1, blood 1.5, fat 3–4 kg · Gain of 1 kg or more in a week with face and hand oedema: suspect pre-eclampsia
Normal values in pregnancy

Hb: 11 or more (10.5 in the second and third trimester) · WBC: up to 15, up to 25 in labour · Platelets below 100: think HELLP or pre-eclampsia · Fibrinogen 4–6 g/L: 2 g/L during PPH means consumption (DIC) · Creatinine below 75 µmol/L · Uric acid lower; rises in pre-eclampsia · ALP up to 4 times · ESR up to 70 mm/h

sc: Fibrinogen 2 g/L during PPH → Not reassuring: consumption (DIC), replace it
